name: Glass widgets
what: Frosted glass phone widgets float round your head - a big number counting up, a render bar filling, your name and handle, a mini views page with growing bars, a now-editing player, a calendar day and a 4K ring closing - with a small glass pill under your chin (Edited with MotionLab). They pop in one after another, bob gently while you talk and shrink away at the end. Simple = three widgets and the pill.
origin: MotionLab's own build after a design in Vibha Ramprakash's claude-video-effects (MIT), 2026-10-28
motion: the widgets pop in one after another, one every 2.1 f from f0 (full: 7 widgets + the pill by f15; simple: 3 + the pill by f7), each from 60 % with an overshoot over 10 f (slow end) and seen within 2 f; while they hold each bobs 6 px on its own phase (one cycle every 1.8 s); inside them the number counts up f4-f22 (S-curve), the views bars grow f10-f33 one after another (12 f each, slow end), the calendar's event slides out f14-f22, the 4K ring closes f12-f42 (S-curve), the render bar fills over 85 % of the length (S-curve) and the player's bar runs to the end (linear, a playback), its icon turning slowly; a band of light crosses the pill f30-f48 (S-curve); the last 8-11 f they shrink to 86 % and fade, the first one first (accelerating)
